title: Circuit Card Inspector - 2nd Shift
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Circuit Card Inspector in Oldsmar, FL for a contract role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company.

The Circuit Card Inspector will visually inspect solder and conformal coating on circuit card assemblies in accordance with IPC-A-610 and J-STD-001 requirements. This 2nd shift role requires prior solder and coating inspection experience, the ability to read engineering drawings and inspection documentation, strong PC skills, and the ability to pass a required medical exam.

Required Skills

  • 2+ years of solder and conformal coating inspection experience.
  • Prior experience visually inspecting solder connections on surface mount and plated through-hole components.
  • IPC-A-610 experience required.
  • J-STD-001 experience required.
  • Ability to navigate IPC standards and determine accept/reject criteria.
  • Ability to read and interpret drawings, diagrams, parts lists, process instructions, inspection instructions, checklists, IPC manuals, revision control documents, and work instructions.
  • Visual inspection experience.
  • Measuring experience using tools such as dial indicators, preset micrometers, scales, or similar measuring devices.
  • Documentation skills.
  • Proficiency with personal computers.
  • Ability to read and write English.
  • Ability to take and pass a required medical exam.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Team-oriented work style.
  • Ability to communicate quality defects effectively and professionally with operations personnel.

Preferred Skills

  • Circuit card assembly inspection experience.
  • Conformal coating inspection experience.
  • Electronics manufacturing inspection experience.
  • Experience inspecting to manufacturing and industry specifications.
  • Experience working in aerospace, defense, electronics, or high-reliability production environments.

What You’ll Do

  • Visually inspect solder and conformal coating on circuit card assemblies.
  • Inspect work in accordance with IPC-A-610 and J-STD-001 requirements.
  • Review circuit card assemblies against manufacturing and industry specifications.
  • Use inspection methods, operations, and prescribed specifications to determine product acceptability.
  • Read and interpret drawings, diagrams, inspection instructions, checklists, and related reference documents.
  • Use measuring devices such as dial indicators, preset micrometers, scales, and related tools.
  • Identify and communicate solder, coating, documentation, or quality defects.
  • Interface with operations teams professionally when communicating quality issues.
  • Maintain accurate inspection documentation.
  • Complete required prescreening and onboarding requirements.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 2nd shift.
  • Monday–Thursday, 3:30 PM–2:00 AM.
  • Weekend overtime may be required.

Pay

  • $19.00–$28.00/hour

title: Secret-Cleared Materials and Process Engineer
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Secret-Cleared Materials and Process Engineer in Woodland Hills, CA for a contract role supporting Northrop Grumman.

The Materials and Process Engineer will support metallic materials, manufacturing processes, supplier qualification, failure analysis, test programs, and engineering design reviews for aerospace and defense hardware. This onsite role requires aerospace, defense, or high-reliability manufacturing experience, metallurgy knowledge, materials testing experience, manufacturing process knowledge, and an active DoD Secret clearance.

Required Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline, preferably Materials Science and Engineering, with 5+ years of engineering experience; master’s degree with 3+ years; or PhD with 1+ year.
  • Higher-level openings may require 8+ years of engineering experience with a bachelor’s degree, 6+ years with a master’s degree, or 4+ years with a PhD.
  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • Active DoD Secret clearance required.
  • Engineering experience in aerospace, defense, or high-reliability manufacturing environments.
  • Practical knowledge of metallurgy for ferrous and nonferrous alloys.
  • Knowledge of heat treatment basics, corrosion, fatigue fundamentals, and common materials testing methods.
  • Hands-on exposure to metallographic sample preparation and lab techniques such as cutting, polishing, etching, and hardness testing.
  • 2+ years of manufacturing process experience, including machining, forging, forming, fastening, welding/brazing, plating, or coating.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings and specifications related to metallic materials and processing.
  • Ability to support failure analysis for metallic parts and processes.
  • Ability to coordinate lab activities and compile test data for interpretation and disposition.
  • Ability to support supplier qualification, supplier technical inquiries, non-conformance investigations, and corrective action recommendations.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work full-time onsite in Woodland Hills, CA.

Preferred Skills

  • Active Top Secret clearance.
  • Master’s degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, or Polymer Engineering.
  • PhD in Material Science or Materials Engineering.
  • Expert-level first-principles engineering knowledge of metals and materials.
  • Knowledge of physical and mechanical properties and evaluation methods, including tensile strength, hardness, fatigue, fracture toughness, creep, stress rupture, SEM, non-destructive inspection, and spectroscopy.
  • Detailed knowledge of production processes such as forging, casting, forming, coating, plating, heat treating, fusion welding, friction stir welding, electron beam welding, additive manufacturing, or composite manufacturing.
  • Hands-on experience in a high-production manufacturing environment.
  • Experience reviewing materials processing and understanding how process variables affect material performance.
  • Experience mentoring or developing employees.
  • Strong ability to communicate technical concepts across all organizational levels.
  • Experience working in fast-paced environments with tight timelines and aggressive schedules.

What You’ll Do

  • Support engineering requirements for parts, materials, processes, manufacturing technologies, machinery, tools, and automation systems.
  • Recommend materials and processes used in product design and manufacturing.
  • Qualify new materials, parts, and processes to meet contractual, regulatory, and technical requirements.
  • Manage or support test and audit programs for supplier qualification.
  • Support engineering design reviews.
  • Participate in failure analysis for metallic parts and processes.
  • Assist with supplier qualification activities and respond to supplier technical inquiries.
  • Analyze tool, material, part, or process failures and recommend corrective actions.
  • Coordinate lab activities including metallography, hardness testing, tensile testing, and NDT/NDI.
  • Compile test data for interpretation and disposition.
  • Support creation and revision of material/process specifications, work instructions, and test plans.
  • Investigate non-conformances and supplier deviations.
  • Collect evidence, support root-cause analysis, and draft corrective action recommendations.
  • Maintain engineering records such as test reports and engineering orders.
  • Support configuration control and design review activity.
  • Communicate technical findings to cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
  • Interact with manufacturing floors, supplier facilities, and testing laboratories.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 9x80 A schedule.
  • Full-time, 40 hours per week.
  • Onsite role.
  • Occasional travel to supplier sites, test facilities, or other company locations may be required.

Pay

  • $89.52/hour

title: Material Handler
description:
PGS Worldwide is seeking a Material Handler in Endicott, NY for a 5-month contract to hire role supporting a leading aerospace & defense company.

The Material Handler will support stockroom, receiving, inventory, kitting, material movement, paperwork inspection, and electronic transaction activity in a manufacturing and warehouse environment. This role requires stockroom or receiving experience, computer data entry skills, inventory accuracy, basic math skills, and the ability to lift up to 50 lbs frequently.

Required Skills

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • Experience in industrial manufacturing, stockkeeping, receiving, warehousing, material handling, or a related environment.
  • Ability to work in a manufacturing and warehousing environment.
  • Ability to operate a hand jack.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs frequently.
  • Computer literacy for data entry, product status updates, and time entry.
  • Ability to read and fully understand written instructions in English.
  • Ability to follow work instructions unless authorized to deviate.
  • Ability to handle materials according to required handling procedures.
  • Ability to review and input required data into computer systems.
  • Basic math skills, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and percentage calculations.
  • Ability to perform and understand required measurements and dimensions.
  • Ability to read and understand engineering drawings and blueprints.
  • Knowledge of, or ability to learn, electrostatic discharge requirements for manufacturing or material handling.
  • Ability to understand statistical process control data.
  • Strong hand-eye coordination and visual acuity.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in a team environment.
  • Reasoning ability to solve problems involving several variables.
  • Ability to manage conflict and participate in team activities.
  • Ability and willingness to recommend process improvements.

Preferred Skills

  • Stockroom experience.
  • Receiving experience.
  • Inventory control experience.
  • Kitting or piece-part picking experience.
  • Experience performing electronic stockkeeping transactions.
  • Experience with ESD equipment or ESD-controlled material handling.
  • Experience using hand tools such as soldering irons, screwdrivers, crimpers, tweezers, scalpels, scissors, microscopes, vices, or thermal strippers.
  • Experience supporting aerospace, defense, electronics manufacturing, or high-reliability production environments.

What You'll Do

  • Handle materials and parts in a stockroom and receiving environment.
  • Sort packages and perform electronic material transactions.
  • Maintain inventory accuracy.
  • Count parts and complete required paperwork.
  • Perform paperwork inspection and communicate with other internal groups.
  • Perform stockkeeping tasks and stockkeeping transactions.
  • Support basic to moderately complex troubleshooting and data manipulation.
  • Follow material plans to pick and prepare parts for distribution to the floor or stockroom operations.
  • Put away parts, fill bins, pick piece parts into kits, and prepare materials for distribution.
  • Move product from one stage to the next step in the manufacturing process.
  • Use tools and devices required by assembly or material handling instructions.
  • Maintain required certifications through hands-on training, written tests, work sample review, and visual examination.
  • Follow required handling, ESD, safety, and process requirements.

Work Schedule / Shift

  • 1st shift.
  • Monday–Friday.
  • Typical hours are 7:30 AM–4:00 PM.
  • Full-time, 40 hours per week.
  • Overtime expected as needed.
  • No travel required.

Pay

  • $17.22/hour
